records.title: Who is doing this, and on whose money
records.text: About this chapter | Claremore | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Claremore, OK of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → About · Claremore, OK Who is doing this, and on whose money This is the Claremore chapter of the Move Weight Foundation , a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. It is independent of the City of Claremore, of Rogers County, and of the State of Oklahoma. It takes no money from any of them. How we source claims Every factual claim on this site links to a primary document or to a named outlet. Where a document exists, we publish the document rather than our description of it. We never invent a government phone number, address or docket number. Every contact datum is transcribed from an official published source and dated on the page. If we have not transcribed it yet, the page says so and links to the city's own directory instead of guessing. Every external link is fetched before it is published , and re-checked automatically every week. The result of that check is public on the automation page . Sources for this chapter were last verified 2026-07-26 . We publish released records whole. No redaction of a public record the government has already released. We never allege a crime. We publish the document, the amount and the date, and let readers and prosecutors do their own jobs. A submitter's identity is never published — not in a page, not in a filename, not in file metadata. We link out to local news and never republish it. What this chapter is not It is not a newspaper, not a campaign, and not aligned with any candidate, party or slate. It does not endorse. Its output is records, an archive, and the plain fact of whether a public body answered a lawful request on time. Funding The Foundation is funded by individual donations. Records cost money — Oklahoma allows a body to charge for search and copying under § 24A.5(3), and a single large request can run into real numbers. Donations pay those invoices, the servers that hold the archive, and nothing else. Contributions are tax-deductible. Zelle: team@moveweight.com . Financial disclosures and the Form 990 are published by the Foundation at foundation.moveweight.com . Corrections If something here is wrong, we want to fix it and we will say that we did. Send the correction and, if you have it, the document — here . A correction is never quietly edited in; the change and its date stay on the page. Contact Records and requests: foia@moveweight.com Everything else: expose@moveweight.net

This page reports what actually happened, including when it failed. A site that quietly rots looks identical to one that is current, right up until somebody relies on it. records.title: Every official link, in one place
records.summary: Verified links to Claremore city government, Rogers County offices, records portals, budgets and Oklahoma oversight bodies. Checked 2026-07-26.
records.text: Claremore City Desk — every official link in one place | Claremore | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content Records & transparency City & Court Clerk The Clerk is the records custodian; minutes not posted online are obtained here. https://claremore.com/city-and-court-clerk/ Claremore budget book The City's published budget, hosted on ClearGov. https://city-claremore-ok-budget-book.cleargov.com/20382 County & state Rogers County https://www.rogerscounty.org/ Oklahoma State Auditor & Inspector https://www.sai.ok.gov/ Oklahoma oversight Where a Claremore decision gets reviewed by somebody who does not work for Claremore. Oklahoma Attorney General Issues Open Records Act opinions. Oklahoma has no free citizen appeal forum — enforcement is a district-court action under § 24A.17. Oklahoma State Auditor & Inspector Audits every county and, on petition or request, municipalities. Published audits are public records. Meetings, and how to be in the room Claremore publishes its agendas through tribe_events : https://claremore.com/city-council/agendas-minutes/ Agendas are posted ahead of the meeting because the law requires it. That posting is the single most useful document in local government and almost nobody opens it — it is where a contract award, a rate change or a tax abatement appears in public for the first time, usually as one line in a consent agenda. Reading a consent agenda Items on a consent agenda are voted through together, with no discussion, in a few seconds. That is not a trick — it is how a body gets through routine business. But it means the only chance to see an item is before the meeting, in the packet. Any member can pull an item out for discussion, and so can a resident who asks one in time. Where to watch → Open the agenda portal → A link that does not work Cities move pages. Every link on this page is re-checked automatically each week and the result is published on the automation page . If one is broken and we have not caught it, tell us .

records.title: A small city with a utility, an authority, and no newsroom
records.summary: A small city with a utility, an authority, and no newsroom — a Move Weight Foundation chapter covering Claremore, Rogers County. File a records request, read the agendas, watch the meetings.
records.text: Claremore, OK — public records and meeting archive Skip to content Why Claremore Claremore runs its own municipal utility and a set of public trusts and authorities that meet separately from the Council. Small cities are not less accountable because less happens — they are less accountable because nobody attends. The agendas are posted 48 hours ahead under the Open Meeting Act; almost nobody reads them. The Move Weight Foundation's first chapter is a town of thirteen thousand people in Ottawa County, Oklahoma, and it now holds 522 archived meetings with machine transcripts. The second is San Angelo, Texas. The third is Southaven, Mississippi, where the City's own released documents show an ad valorem agreement abating two thirds of property tax on a recital of twenty new jobs. None of those started with a tip. They started with somebody reading the agenda. If you already know something Send it anonymously . A submitter's identity is never published — not in a page, not in a filename, not in metadata.

records.summary: Local and statewide newsrooms covering Claremore and Oklahoma. We link out; we never republish another newsroom
records.text: Claremore news & allies | Claremore | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content Why we link instead of republish Local newsrooms are paid by attention. An aggregator that lifts a paragraph and keeps the reader on its own page takes that attention and gives nothing back, and then the newsroom shrinks and there is less reporting for everyone — including for us, because most of what a records request confirms was first noticed by a reporter. So the rule here is absolute: link out, never republish . The only documents hosted on this site are public records, which belong to the public already. Working on Claremore? If you are a reporter, a nonprofit or a resident group working on something here, the archive and the request pipeline are yours to use, and we will file on your behalf if a request under your own name would cost you something. Get in touch .

records.title: File a request the city has to answer
records.summary: How to file a public records request with the City of Claremore under 51 O.S. § 24A.1 et seq. — the deadline, the fees, the appeal, and a letter you can copy.
records.text: File a Oklahoma Open Records Act request in Claremore | Claremore | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content Build your letter This runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type here is sent anywhere, stored, or seen by us — copy the result and send it yourself from your own email. Your name Your email What you are asking for Date range Ask for electronic delivery Require a cost estimate before charges Require an itemised legal basis for anything withheld Copy the letter Write the request narrow, then widen it “All emails about the project” gets refused as overbroad and burns your deadline. “Emails between the City Manager and [named party] between 1 March and 30 April” gets answered. Once you see what came back, ask again with what you learned. Two narrow requests beat one that never gets filled. Where to send it Claremore's own records channel is listed on the City Desk , with the exact URL the City publishes. Use it — a request filed through the body's own portal is the hardest one for it to say it never received. Send a copy to foia@moveweight.com at the same time. We log the send date, watch the deadline, and if it lapses we publish that fact. A request nobody knows about is a request the city can ignore quietly. Track the clock § 24A.5 gives the City prompt, reasonable time. Put the send date in your calendar with that many days added, and put a second reminder a week later. Most requests are not denied — they are simply never answered, and the only thing that changes that is somebody noticing on the exact day. If you are refused Oklahoma has no administrative appeal and no fixed deadline — only a “prompt, reasonable” standard, which makes delay the default tactic. Enforcement is a civil action in district court under 51 O.S. § 24A.17, and a requester who prevails can recover attorney fees, which is what makes the remedy usable at all. Because the deadline is a standard rather than a number, a dated written record of every follow-up is the case. Keep the refusal Whatever the outcome, keep the exact wording of the denial and the date. A refusal that cites no statute, or cites one that does not apply, is itself the story — and it is the document an appeal turns on.

records.title: A small city with a utility, an authority, and no newsroom
records.summary: The structural question this chapter was opened on, the specific public record that answers it, and what has been asked for so far.
records.text: What we are asking Claremore | Claremore | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Claremore, OK of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → The Question · Claremore, OK A small city with a utility, an authority, and no newsroom Claremore runs its own municipal utility and a set of public trusts and authorities that meet separately from the Council. Small cities are not less accountable because less happens — they are less accountable because nobody attends. The agendas are posted 48 hours ahead under the Open Meeting Act; almost nobody reads them. This is a question, not an accusation No one at this Foundation has alleged that anybody in Claremore has done anything wrong, and nothing on this site should be read that way. Chapters are opened on structural risk — large capital programmes, fast growth, a single dominant employer, a utility or authority that meets away from the council — because those are the conditions under which decisions get made with nobody watching. That is a statement about attention, not about anybody's conduct. Naming a city next to an accusation we have not documented would be precisely the thing this project exists to oppose. So the page you are reading names the question and the record that settles it, and then we go and ask for the record. The record that answers it Claremore Public Works Authority and Industrial/Economic Development Authority agendas, minutes and utility rate ordinances. How this gets resolved Ask. A request goes to the City of Claremore under 51 O.S. § 24A.1 et seq.. The City has prompt, reasonable time. Publish what comes back, whole. Released public records go up unredacted. We do not summarise a document in place of showing it, and we do not redact what the government already released. Publish what does not come back. A missed deadline, a refusal with no statute cited, an estimate that prices a resident out — those get published too, with dates. Silence is a finding. Rewrite this page. When the documents are in, this page stops being a question and becomes what the records showed — including if they showed nothing. A chapter that only ever reports wrongdoing is not doing arithmetic, it is doing marketing. What you can do right now You do not need us. The statute is yours, and a request from a resident of Claremore is harder to wave away than one from a nonprofit two states over. records.title: Watch your government
records.summary: Where to watch Claremore government on video — meeting recordings, agendas, and the archives that keep them after the city takes them down.
records.text: Watch your government | Claremore | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Claremore, OK of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Video · Claremore, OK Watch your government Almost every decision that costs you money is made in a room with a camera in it. The recordings are public. Most people never find them because they are buried three clicks deep on a government site. Here they are. Where the video lives These are Claremore's own recordings and portals. We link to them rather than rehosting, so you are watching the authoritative copy. City of Claremore on YouTube City of Claremore The City's own channel, linked from the City's homepage. Open → We link, we do not rehost These are the government's own recordings on the government's own platforms. We send you there rather than mirroring them, so you are watching the authoritative copy and the view count lands where it belongs. The exception is when a recording disappears — see below. When a recording goes missing Meeting video gets taken down. Sometimes it is a retention policy, sometimes a platform migration, sometimes nobody can say why. Either way the public record evaporates, and the one meeting you needed is the one that is gone. That is why the Foundation's Miami, Oklahoma chapter keeps 522 meetings archived with machine transcripts and captions , mirrored to the Internet Archive. It is the deepest archive we run and the model for every other chapter. See what a full archive looks like → If you spot a gap A meeting with no video, a recording that ends mid-item, a link that used to work — tell us . A missing recording is itself a records request: the city holds the raw file whether or not it publishes it, and we will ask for it. Getting more out of a meeting recording Read the agenda packet first. It usually contains the actual contract or ordinance. The video is people discussing a document you can already have in front of you. Note the timestamp of anything that matters. A citation like "14 January, 1:42:10" is something a reporter or an auditor can verify in a minute. Watch the vote, not the speech. Who moved it, who seconded, who was absent, and whether it was on a published agenda. Executive session is a flag, not a crime. Bodies may close a meeting for defined reasons and must certify which. If a payment or a contract was discussed behind a closed door, the certification is a public record. Ask for it → Follow this chapter No social accounts yet for this chapter. We publish to the site first. Social accounts are a distribution channel, never the record — anything we post there exists here with its source document attached.
